semester: 5th Semester (Winter Term Start); 6th Semester (Summer Term Start)

learning_outcomes.text: Students can systematically structure, plan, and accompany a project in every phase of project management.
They confidently apply the process model according to DIN 69901.
They use proven methods and procedural models and purposefully integrate important success factors of project management into their project planning and execution.
Students analyze deficits and potential for improvement in project organizations and develop implementable measures to address these problems and optimize processes.
Students develop and implement comprehensive risk management strategies to identify, assess, and minimize potential project risks.
Students use project management software tools in SMEs to efficiently plan, control, and monitor projects.
In conjunction with their own project experience, students can successfully fulfill the role of project manager for small to medium-sized projects.

syllabus_topics: What is a project? Why do projects fail (project pathology)? Importance of project work in the VUCA world
Project initialization: Idea, goals, assignment, management systems, phase models, milestones, quality gates, procedural models, agile project management
Project definition: Organization and roles, people and leadership, effort estimation, risk management, business case, contract management
Project planning: Project structure plan, project schedule, network planning technique, resource plan, cost planning, change request management, quality management

Project control: Meeting management, kick-off meeting, work techniques, management cycle, deadline control and MTA, deviations and measures, project controlling, communication management, crisis management
Project closure: Project closure report, project acceptance, lessons learned, further processes
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam. The grade's weight for the final grade is determined by the credit points.
